source_topology_binding.source_only_bridge_analysis: The stochastic identity is for each fixed evaluation time, not automatically one common full-measure event for all times. Source keeps this scope.

source_evidence.anchor: Original Samplinglib supplement: Use a past event on one Itô cell. Exact assumptions and formula below.
source_evidence.statement: Restrict a progressive integrand to the cell (s,t] and an event known at s. The restricted process is progressive and square integrable. Its completed Itô integral at each fixed time is the original cell increment, truncated at that time, multiplied by the event indicator.
source_evidence.formula: \begin{gathered}\theta_r(\omega)=\mathbf1_A(\omega)\mathbf1_{\{s<r\le t\}}\eta_r(\omega)\quad\text{for all }r,\omega,\\ I_u(\theta)=\mathbf1_A\bigl(I_{t\wedge u}(\eta)-I_{s\wedge u}(\eta)\bigr)\quad\mu\text{-a.e. for each fixed }u\le T.\end{gathered}
assumptions: A progressive, real, product-space L² integrand on a positive deterministic horizon T with finite sample measure μ.
One scalar Brownian motion under μ relative to the given filtration. The filtration satisfies the usual conditions.
The deterministic endpoints satisfy 0 ≤ s ≤ t ≤ T.
The event A is measurable in the filtration at time s. The evaluation time u is any fixed time in [0,T].
source_evidence.boundary: The integral identity is for each deterministic evaluation time. The restriction of the integrand is pointwise.

steps.title: Switch between two stopping times
steps.text: Take the stop to be t on A and s on its complement. The event and its complement are already known at s, so Mathlib's piecewise constant theorem applies.
steps.assessment: The stated mathematical move and formula agree with the current proof and its hypotheses.

steps.title: Subtract the two closed stopped inputs
steps.text: Subtract the input stopped at s from the input stopped at the switch. This yields the exact pointwise event and cell restriction.
steps.assessment: The stated mathematical move and formula agree with the current proof and its hypotheses.

steps.title: Use linearity and stopping compatibility
steps.text: The completed integral of the difference equals the difference of the two completed stopped integrals. Evaluate each one at the capped time.
